stale-text-alternative-on-dynamic-named-.mechanism: F20 on the icon-only repeat-MODE cycle button (button#repeatBtn): its entire accessible name is the inline <svg><title id='repeatTitle'>, with no visible text or aria-label to dilute it. Each click cycles off→all→one, morphing the glyph (loop recolor, '1' overlay) and updating the visible caption, but the handler rewrites the <title> only on the first transition (off→all), so from the second click the name is frozen one state behind — e.g. glyph/caption read 'Repeat one track' while the announced name stays 'Repeat all tracks'.
stale-text-alternative-on-dynamic-named-.scenario: Tideline ambient-music player (lang='en'): an icon-only repeat-mode cycle button whose sole accessible name is its <svg><title>. After the second click the glyph and visible caption show 'Repeat one track' but the <svg><title> (the whole name) is still 'Repeat all tracks', so AT announces the previous mode.
stale-text-alternative-on-dynamic-named-.note: Wrong page entirely: scenario describes an Arabic RTL developer-forum flag/report toggle (button#flagBtn, <svg><title id='flagTitle'>, name 'أبلغ عن هذه المشاركة' / 'تراجع'), but the real page is an English LTR music player with a 3-state repeat-mode cycle button#repeatBtn / title#repeatTitle. Same F20-via-<svg><title> mechanism, but different topic, language, selector, glyph, and frozen string.

multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous/case-.mechanism: F86 Example 3 (label associated with the first part only). The price-range filter is one 'from–to' value in two boxes: the visible 'Price range' is a <label for='price-min'> naming ONLY the minimum box, while the maximum box's only associated label is the en-dash separator (<label for='price-max'>–</label>), so its computed accessible name is the lone character '–'. The maximum sub-field therefore has no name identifying it as a price field — a multi-part field whose parts are not differentiated.
multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous/case-.scenario: Holloway & Pike Lettings rental search (lang='en'): a 'Price range (per month)' filter as two boxes '$ ___ – $ ___'. The minimum box (#price-min) is named 'Price range'; the maximum box (#price-max) is labelled only by the en-dash separator, so AT names it '–', failing to identify the maximum-price field.
multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous/case-.note: Wrong page and wrong mechanism: scenario describes a Japanese municipal postal-code (郵便番号) entered as a 3-digit + 4-digit pair, both carrying the identical aria-label='郵便番号' (the 'all parts share one identical name' variant). The real page is an English rental price-range filter whose failure is F86 Example 3 — label tied to the first box, second box named by its separator '–'. The aspect (undifferentiated multi-part sub-names) genuinely holds, but the concrete instance, selector, and sub-mechanism differ.

multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous/case-.mechanism: A compound delivery phone is split into three boxes (country code, area code, local number). Each box has a VISIBLE caption beside it (a plain <span class='cap'>) that is never associated (no for=, aria-label, or aria-labelledby), so the only accessible-name source on each input is its placeholder format mask. The computed names are therefore '+##', '###', and '#### ####' — masks that do not identify which part is the country code, area code, or local number (F86, compounded by F111 since the visible captions are absent from the names).
multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous/case-.scenario: Posthaven Courier shipping label (lang='en'): a 'Delivery contact phone' field as three boxes (country code / area code / local number). Each input's only accessible name is its placeholder mask ('+##', '###', '#### ####'); the visible captions are unassociated spans, so AT names the boxes by their digit masks rather than their roles.
multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous/case-.note: Wrong page and wrong mechanism: scenario describes a Northgate Cardiology blood-pressure reading (systolic input, diastolic input, unit <select>) where all three controls share title='Blood pressure'. The real page is a courier phone field whose parts are named by their placeholder format masks (unassociated visible captions). The aspect (ambiguous/undifferentiated multi-part sub-names) genuinely holds, but topic, selector, and the concrete naming mechanism differ.
